root_motivation: **Who:** Joe, who will read feedback once a day; synthorg, which will turn themes into seeds; the agent, whose single line should land next to 11 others saying the same thing. **What:** a theme table with counts and evidence, an admin verb, a counts-only public field. **Why not today:** `feedback` rows (PRD-mcphost-feedback-tool-and-ledger) are flat; `admin.*` verbs (`admin.rs`: 20 verbs, `admin.status.rollup` the closest) expose no feedback; `/status.json` (`statusfeed.rs`) carries component uptime only. An LLM clusterer would make the theme list a prompt-injection surface; the standing rule is quoted data, never instructions. **Premise (creative):** normalized text + code + tool is enough to cluster. **Falsifier:** AC 1 runs the 10-08 error corpus through the normalizer and asserts 4–20 themes.
user_persona: An agent that calls host.state.delete_rows with an empty filter on a 5 000-row table, reads confirm_required.dry_run_first, runs the dry run, notices the empty filter and fixes it; a Claude Code user who sees a destructive marker on host.table.drop.

acceptance_criteria.description: Given the 56 live error texts of the 10-08 chain stored as a fixture with their codes and tools, When `normalize` and the key are applied, Then the theme count is between 4 and 20, proving the LLM-free key separates asks.

Given two rows with texts `args_invalid said 4.78 is not an integer` and `args_invalid says 12.5 is not an integer` on the same tool, When clustered, Then they share one `theme_id` with `count: 2` and both ids in `example_ids`.
Given rows with the same text but different `error_code`, When clustered, Then they land in different themes.
Given a clustered table, When the nightly task runs again with no new rows, Then no theme row changes (`count`, `last_seen`, `example_ids` identical) and 0 `feedback` rows are updated.
Given `MCPHOST_ADMIN_KEY` and 3 themes, When `admin.feedback.themes {since:"7d"}` is called, Then 3 themes come back sorted by `count` desc and a call without the key returns `unauthorized`.
Given `/status.json`, When parsed, Then `feedback` has exactly the keys `rows_24h` and `themes_open`, both integers.

Given a tenant that filed `f_a` and another that filed `f_b`, When the first calls `host.feedback.get {feedback_id:"f_b"}`, Then the code is `feedback_not_found`; `f_a` returns `theme_id` and `status: "open"` after clustering.

Given prod after deploy and one planted feedback filed the previous day, When the nightly task has run, Then `/status.json.feedback.themes_open ≥ 1` (Live; evidence: `ssh orch 'curl -s https://www.mcphost.dev/status.json | python3 -c "import json,sys; print(json.load(sys.stdin)[\"feedback\"])"'`)
acceptance_criteria.test: deferred -- operator-provisioned: Live check of prod /status.json after deploy and a planted feedback row filed the previous day.

scope: src/confirm.rs (new): the gated set derived from WRITE_VERBS, token mint/hash, canonical args hash, confirm_required/confirm_invalid errors.
src/handler.rs: dispatch gate (dry-run measure, token check, scratch bypass), destructiveHint annotations and description suffix in host_tools.
non_goals: Human approval; gating scratch tenants; gating host.key.rotate and host.self.offboard; changing what any verb does once confirmed.

additional.token_never_stored: only sha256(token) is stored; the token is shown once by the dry run.

five_whys_trace.q: Why can an agent delete 5 000 rows by accident?
five_whys_trace.a: dry_run is optional and nobody is required to read it.
Prose at a boundary is skipped; a refusal carrying the exact dry-run call cannot be.

five_whys_trace.q: Why bind the token to args and diff?
five_whys_trace.a: A token for another filter or another state would authorise a different delete.

ambiguities_resolved.question: Which diffs are gated?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: A dry-run diff with a measurable row count (rows[].delete, tables[].rows) at or above plan confirm_rows_min; verbs that report no count are not gated yet.

ambiguities_resolved.question: Token bound to key or session?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: Tenant (key hash), per the PRD default.
